topic: Texas transplant reality check: pick the city before the house
hook: The house is the last thing you should pick.

scores.worst_problem: The hook states a familiar real-estate truism ('location before house'), so a reader can half-guess the payoff without swiping.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold a Texas-specific consequence instead of the generic principle — e.g. 'Four filters run before the house. Skip the third and it costs you every month.'

deck.topic: Texas transplant reality check: pick the city before the house
deck.hook: The house is the last thing you should pick.

points.title: Summer Owns Your Day
body: June through September, real life happens before ten or after eight.
Locals plan around shade the way other states plan around snow.

points.title: Twenty Minutes Is Fiction
body: That twenty minute drive across Austin at 8am is closer to fifty.
San Antonio loops move better. In DFW, distance is honest distance and there is a lot of it.

points.title: No Income Tax, But
body: Texas takes it back through property tax and insurance, and the rate changes by county and district.
Two houses at the same price can carry very different yearly costs.

points.title: School Zones Get Redrawn
body: Districts grow fast here and attendance boundaries move with them.
The campus everyone raved about three years ago may not be the one you are zoned to today.

points.title: Weekends Have A Radius
body: From San Antonio you are ninety minutes from river country and a morning from the coast.
Austin trades that for lake and greenbelt. DFW weekends point at lakes and a longer drive to get anywhere else.

points.title: Run It This Way
body: City first. Then commute. Then the tax and insurance number. Then schools.
The house is what is left standing after those four filters, not the thing you start with.
points.loop: Most people learn this after closing.

linkedinCaption:
Most relocation regret I see in Texas is not about the house. It is about the city, the commute, or the tax line nobody modeled before closing.

Buyers arrive with a price range and a wish list. What actually shapes daily life here is heat that reorders your schedule, traffic that makes twenty minutes a fiction, county and district costs that vary widely at the same purchase price, and school boundaries that move as districts grow.

The order matters. City. Commute. Tax and insurance. Schools. The house is what survives those four filters.

For those of you working with out of state buyers, what part of Texas living do they underestimate most?
